subject: Aurelia Labs - capacity SKU split & scoped change order
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity bump + scope split for Q3 pilot

Avery —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and expect the pilot to need an uplift: roughly +120K tokens/day sustained, with two distinct workloads (inference + embeddings). Our procurement team asked that we surface a simple change order that:

- splits the existing Order Form into two SKUs (inference / embeddings) with separate rate bands,
- adds a temporary burst pool for June-July (estimated 4 gpus equivalent),
- adjusts the monthly minimum for the pilot period and adds a one-time implementation credit if we go live by 2026-07-15.

Can you send a starter change order and an estimated price delta? Also copying our procurement contact (sara@procureteam.com) who will handle PO / payment terms.

Best,
Dana Li
Head of Platform
Aurelia Labs

--
Attachment: expected_usage_q3.xlsx (reference)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>
Cc: ProcureTeam / Sara Kim <sara@procureteam.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity bump + scope split for Q3 pilot

Dana / Sara —

Thanks — super clear. I've drafted a short change order that captures the SKU split, temporary burst pool, and the implementation credit. High-level notes:

- Monthly minimum will be adjusted only for the pilot window (2026-06-01 to 2026-08-31) and then revert to baseline unless we agree a longer term commit.
- Burst pool priced as a time-boxed add-on; we'll offer an introductory burst discount for the first two weeks of ramp.
- Implementation credit: applied against first invoice if customer signs by 2026-07-15.

I've attached "proposed_change_order_v1.pdf". Before I send to procurement/legal on your side, we need internal legal to run a quick redline on three items: SLA (exhibit G) for burst, data residency note for embeddings (Aurelia asked about EU fallback earlier), and invoicing net-terms (ProcureTeam prefers Net 30). Can @irene_choi and @karthik_iyer review for redlines?

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal legal redlines (today)
2) Send redlined CO + Aurelia procurement terms back to Sara for PO alignment (same day)
3) Produce DocuSign after agreement

If that's agreeable I'll loop you all in.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0187

Attachment: proposed_change_order_v1.pdf

From: Sara Kim <sara@procureteam.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity bump + scope split for Q3 pilot / procurement notes

Hi Avery —

Quick items from procurement:
- Standard Aurelia PO terms are Net 30, 1% early pay discount if paid within 10 days.
- We will not accept retroactive price increases that apply before a signed change order date. Please include effective date on the CO.
- Need an export control / data handling memo for embeddings — our security team flagged EU fallback as a gating item.

I attached Aurelia's procurement template (aurelia_procurement_terms.pdf). Happy to review the final CO once we have your redlines.

Sara Kim
Senior Procurement Manager (ProcureTeam, on behalf of Aurelia Labs)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>, ProcureTeam / Sara Kim <sara@procureteam.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Capacity bump + scope split for Q3 pilot — request for legal redlines

Irene / Karthik —

Forwarding Aurelia's ask and Sara's procurement notes below. TL;DR: they're asking for a temporary SKU split + burst pool and an implementation credit tied to a sign-by date. Procurement wants Net 30 and an explicit effective date.

Can legal do a light-weight redline on the attached CO focusing on:
- Exhibit G SLA for burst (we should limit credits to token-level latency thresholds, not availability for burst nodes);
- Data residency fallback language for embeddings — prefer a contract note that we will route embeddings to EU nodes on request but with potential latency/cost implications;
- Effective date language + no retroactive charges before signature;
- Implementation credit accounting (ensure it is a one-time invoice credit, capped).

If you prefer I can propose a tracked-changes doc; otherwise feel free to reply-all with redline notes.

Thanks —
Avery

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>, ProcureTeam / Sara Kim <sara@procureteam.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Capacity bump + scope split for Q3 pilot — redlines attached

Avery —

Quick initial redline summary (see attached "redlines_marked.docx"):

1) SLA / Burst nodes — mark to limit credit exposure: credit only applies for sustained latency SLA misses on production inference routes (not for short-term degradation during burst ramp). Recommend cap: 25% of monthly fee for the burst pool period.
2) Data residency — add clause: customer-requested EU routing for embedding storage/lookup; Redwood will comply where regionally available but reserves the right to adjust pricing for additional hosting costs. Add cross-reference to the Private deployment option in the MSA in case customer requires strict isolation.
3) Effective date / no retroactive charges — add explicit effective date field on CO and a line: "Charges will not be applied for usage prior to the execution date of this Change Order."
4) Implementation credit — specify maximum credit amount and apply to the first invoice after execution. Add audit right for one month to verify go-live date.
5) Procurement terms (Net 30 / early pay) — commercial is fine with Net 30; note procurement-specific indemnity redlines in Aurelia template should be escalated to Legal Ops if they try to push broader IP wording.

Karthik — please confirm whether pricing floor needs sign-off from Revenue Ops. Laura, looping you for a quick sign-off on the credit cap (proposed $12,000).

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_marked.docx (track changes summary)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana@aurelia.ai>, ProcureTeam / Sara Kim <sara@procureteam.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Final: change order + next steps (DocuSign)

Dana / Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Irene's redlines we've:
- capped the burst-credit at $12,000 for the pilot window,
- added explicit effective-date language (charges not applied before execution),
- included the EU routing note for embeddings with a pricing caveat,
- accepted Net 30 (with the early-pay discount clause as optional).

I've uploaded the final, signed-ready change order to DocuSign. Please use the link below to sign so we can activate the burst pool for June 1st:

DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc123

Notes / reminders:
- HubSpot deal HB-SP-2026-0892 has been updated with the CO and JIRA SUP-987 opened to track provisioning work.
- Implementation credit will be applied to the first invoice after go-live and is capped at $12,000.
- If Aurelia needs a Private deployment SKU for GDPR/stringent residency, that will require an additional SOW and longer lead time.

Please reply-all when signed and we will schedule a 30-minute handoff with our provisioning team (cc'd in the JIRA).

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0187
